document.title: Usama bin Laden: Request for Ambassador Level Demarches (State Department Cable 100503)
document.authors: Department of State (Secretary of State Madeleine Albright)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Newly Published Documents Cast Doubt on Claims Taliban Will Give Up al Qaeda | National Security Archive
document.note: [Secret] Albright directs the ambassadors in Abu Dhabi, Riyadh and Islamabad to tell host governments that there is clear and compelling information that bin Laden is planning an attack on US targets. They are to say the Taliban will be held responsible, to urge the Taliban to extradite UBL to a third country, and to ask the UAE to withdraw landing rights for Ariana Airlines until he is extradited.

events.description: State Department cable instructs ambassadors in Abu Dhabi, Riyadh and Islamabad to deliver urgent demarches on bin Ladin's planned attacks and Taliban harboring.
Scheduled meeting of the US Ambassador with Prince Sultan in Riyadh.
State Department cable instructs ambassadors in Abu Dhabi, Riyadh and Islamabad to deliver demarches on bin Ladin's planned attacks and Taliban harboring.
Scheduled US Ambassador meeting with Prince Sultan in Riyadh.

relationships.quote: THEIR PROVISION OF PROTECTION AND SAFEHAVEN TO THIS TERRORIST MURDERER IS UNNACEPTABLE.

relationships.quote: WE KNOW THAT BIN LADIN USES ARIANA TO FACILITATE HIS OPERATIONS.

sources_cited: US State Department cable STATE 100503, 29 May 1999
key_claims: The US had reliable information that bin Ladin was planning near-term attacks on US facilities in the Arabian Peninsula, Africa, South Asia and/or Southeast Asia.
Despite Taliban assurances, bin Ladin and his network were operating freely in Afghanistan.
The US warned it would hold the Taliban directly responsible for any bin Ladin attack and reserved the right to pre-empt or retaliate.
The US demanded the Taliban expel bin Ladin to a third country for justice.
The US asked the UAE and Saudi Arabia to withdraw Ariana Airlines landing rights because bin Ladin uses it for operations.
The US asked Saudi Arabia to urge Pakistan to press the Taliban over bin Ladin.
